blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) in Central Visayas will use its Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning (ARAL) Program to help students who fall behind as repeated face-to-face class suspensions disrupt teacher-led instruction in Cebu. This came as Cebu schools continued to deal with disruptions to face-to-face instruction amid the current haze episode affecting Metro Cebu. Regional Director Arturo Bayocot said that learning would continue during the suspensions through distance-learning modalities and prepared learning modules.
